newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Cypriots protest over British exercises.
newsitem.headline: Cypriots protest over British exercises.

text.p: British forces in Cyprus ignored protests from local environmentalists and carried out military exercises on a remote western peninsula of the Mediterranean island on Thursday, witnesses said.

Local environmentalists want exercises banned and the Akamas area declared a national park. British troops are allowed to train there for up to 70 days a year under the treaty granting the former British colony independence.
The live-fire exercises started on Monday in the rugged area on the northwest coast noted for its natural beauty and wildlife. They are due to end on Friday.
Police blocked groups of women and motorcyclists from approaching the firing site on Thursday. Dozens of cars from nearby villages of the Paphos district were turned back, witnesses said.
Organisers of the protest said a party of less than 30 men had entered the six square km (2.3 square mile) firing range and lit small fires to make the British troops aware of their presence.

"They (the soldiers) knew there were people in the firing range and yet they continued their exercises," said Christos Andreou, a campaigner against British bases in Cyprus. "It is unacceptable and criminal."
A spokesman for the British bases in Cyprus dismissed claims activists were in the area. "We are training as planned," he said.
Earlier in the week a member of parliament said he hid in the firing range for two days in a failed attempt to obstruct the exercises.
